title: Reliability pulseboard handoff notes - 2026-07-18
body:
Quick handoff / prep for weekly SRE ops sync (notes to self).

Meeting goal:
- Surface current SLO health, highlight paging trends, review top 3 incidents in the last 7 days, agree next actions and owners. Keep under 45m.

Snapshot metrics (last 7 days, sampled at midnight UTC):
- API success rate (5xx+4xx aggregated): 99.48% (SLO = 99.9%) -> error budget burn ~0.42% *this week* (cumulative EB burn 12% month-to-date).
- p95 latency (inference): 420ms (SLO p95 < 300ms) — heavy tail correlated with cold KV cache misses and queueing on a specific GC job pattern.
- p99 latency: 1.8s (alert threshold crossed twice last 72h).
- Paging frequency: avg 1.6 pages/day on weekdays; spike to 5 pages last Tue during INC-7543.
- Top offending route: /v1/chat/stream (60% of error volume).

Paging trends notes:
- Most pages are operational (queue/backpressure) not functional regressions. Pattern: batch rebalancer + nightly quantization job cause temporary spike in queue length on hosting nodes in us-west2.
- On-call feedback: pagers between 02:00-04:30 UTC are noisy and repeatedly wake the same person. Need rotation or escalation policy tweak.

Top incidents (TL;DR):
1) INC-7543 - KV-cache queue backlog -> externalization to fallback model; lasted 38m; root cause: unexpected job overlap (rebalancer + heavy prefix-populate jobs). Mitigations: temporary autoscale bump, rollout of backpressure controls. Follow-up: finalize rate-limiter in serving runtime (PR referenced).
2) INC-7560 - Degraded p95 on /v1/chat/stream during canary rollout of runtime kernel selector; lasted 45m; root cause: kernel selection fallback path invoked more often than expected for long-seq clients. Follow-up: add telemetry to selector decision path + tighten canary config.
3) INC-7592 - Spurious 429s from quota system during quota-sync lag; lasted 12m; root cause: retry storm from legacy client. Follow-up: temporary tweak to quota-sync job + client library fix.

Runbook gaps observed:
- KV-cache queueing runbook lacks clear escalation matrix and no playbook for temporary autoscale bump.
- Canary rollback checklist missing step to revert kernel-selector config in control plane.

Discussion points for sync:
- Short-term: bump autoscaler cooldown to avoid oscillations (proposal: 2m -> 6m).
- Medium: land PR #1824 (serving runtime rate limiter) and schedule canary with tighter guardrails.
- Longer: reserve dedicated small pool for prefix-populate jobs or move them to off-peak window.
- On-call: propose 1-week trial of 8-hour awake window and an overflow pager for second responder.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Avery: draft autoscaler cooldown RFC + perf analysis by 2026-07-22.
- Samir: finish telemetry for kernel-selector and post a short rollforward plan (due 2026-07-21).
- Lucia: update KV-cache runbook with autoscale play and escalation steps; ping SRE leads for review by 2026-07-23.
- Platform eng (assign TBD): schedule prefix-populate job to off-peak or allocate dedicated pool; proposal due 2026-07-30.
- Oncall rotation owner (Ben): pilot overflow pager + updated shift guidelines; start pilot 2026-07-25.

Loose notes / ideas to bring up:
- Could we add a "soft-fuse" in the control plane to throttle prefix-populate for a tenant if queue latency crosses p95 threshold?
- Consider a daily short report emailed to eng leads highlighting any pages >30m and action owners.
- Evaluate whether the quota-sync lag 429s would be prevented by client-side jitter/randomized retry backoff (ask SDK team).

Questions for leads during sync:
- Product: are we ok shifting some non-essential background jobs out of peak region windows?
- Infra: any objections to a small reserved pool for heavy prefix population?
- Observability: can we add a high-cardinality tag for kernel-selector decisions to correlate with client seq-lengths?

Post-meeting quick follow-up template (to copy/paste):
- Summary (1-2 lines): 
- Key decisions: 
- Owners + due dates: 
- Links: incident, PRs, runbook pages

Notes to self: keep this one-page and pragmatic. Call out people explicitly when assigning tasks in Slack after the meeting. Avoid action items with vague owners ("platform eng" should be replaced with a named person before EOD).

End of notes.
